title.en: Keep the construction parameters, not the mesh

summary: Hold the defining parameters of a geometric construction as state and rebuild the mesh from them on every change.
objective: Make a geometry scene answer questions about its construction rather than only display a shape.
applies_when: A shape is defined by a construction, such as a cutting plane, a profile, a radius or a set of points.
The viewer can change a parameter and expects the shape and the derived values to follow.
Measurements, intersections or classifications are displayed with the shape.
intent_signals: let me move the cutting plane
example_prompts: Let me tilt the plane through the cone and see the section change.
Change the profile and rebuild the solid of revolution.
negative_signals: Imported or sculpted meshes with no generating construction.
Static illustrations where no parameter is exposed.
not_for: Imported or sculpted meshes with no generating construction.
Static illustrations where no parameter is exposed.

principles: In a construction scene the parameters are the subject and the mesh is a rendering of them. Editing vertices detaches the picture from the mathematics that is supposed to explain it.
Derived values must come from the parameters through the same path as the geometry, otherwise a label can report a number that the shape no longer has.
Regeneration makes boundary and degenerate cases reachable, which is where the mathematics is most instructive and where an edited mesh silently fails.
Tessellation quality is a display parameter and should be separable from the construction, so refining the mesh does not change the model.
implementation: Store the construction inputs, such as plane normal and offset, radii, control points or an interval, as the authoritative state.
Rebuild geometry and every derived quantity from those inputs, and keep the rebuild cheap enough to run on each change.

Expose tessellation density as its own control and state, for each displayed quantity, whether it is analytic from the parameters or sampled from the mesh; analytic values should not move under refinement and sampled ones should be shown converging.
Handle the degenerate parameter values explicitly in the rebuild instead of allowing the mesh builder to produce a broken shape.
Persist the parameters, not the vertices, when the scene is saved or shared.
observable_checks: Change one parameter and confirm the shape, the labels and the derived numbers all update together.

Refine the tessellation and confirm quantities computed from the mesh converge, while quantities computed analytically from the parameters stay unchanged. A readout that moves when only the display resolution changes is either a sampled quantity, which should say so, or an analytic quantity wrongly derived from the mesh.
Reload from the stored state and confirm an identical construction.
Drive a parameter to a boundary value and confirm the rebuild handles it deliberately.

creative_affordances: The visual treatment of a construction, including ghosted history and animated regeneration, is entirely free.
Sculpted decoration can be layered over a parametric core when the two are separated.
known_limits: Authored state-model guidance; no runtime scene has been rebuilt or measured for this record.
It does not prescribe a modelling kernel or a tessellation algorithm.
